stories.headline: WA police appeal for help to find 10-year-old girl missing from Perth suburbs

opening: Lyndel Ningella was last seen leaving home in Butler on Saturday evening prompting concerns about her safety Western Australia police have appealed for help in finding a 10-year-old girl who went missing from Perth’s outer northern suburbs on Saturday.
Lyndel Ningella has not been seen since early Saturday evening when police said the young girl was seen leaving a home in Butler at about 5:45pm on 15 August.

stories.title: How U.S. military funding propelled China’s robot dogs
stories.summary: WASHINGTON, Aug 18 - China’s Unitree Robotics – among the world's biggest producers of humanoid and quadruped robots – based designs for its most successful robot dogs on innovations funded by the U.S. military, according to a former U.S. defense technology official and three top researchers involved in the project.
article_sentences: China’s Unitree Robotics – among the world's biggest producers of humanoid and quadruped robots – based designs for its most successful robot dogs on innovations funded by the U.S. military, according to a former U.S. defense technology official and three top researchers involved in the project.
Unitree’s $1,600 Go2 model, launched in 2023, helped the company rapidly dominate the global quadruped robot market — its.
Shanghai IPO has drawn frenzied demand.
Another Unitree robot has been shown on Chinese state television, armed and accompanying People’s Liberation Army (PLA) troops on an exercise.
These robots draw on breakthroughs in quadruped movement financed by the U.S. DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory (ARL) and other military programs, the researchers and the former official told Reuters.
The Army-funded project turned into, “basically, the first Unitree robot that had any kind of scale," said Gavin Kenneally, a former University of Pennsylvania researcher involved in the program.

Ben Katz, who worked at Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s Biomimetic Robotics Lab, among a consortium of universities financed by the military programs, said the dimensions of Unitree’s popular Go series were “to the millimeter” almost identical to a groundbreaking robot he helped develop called Mini Cheetah.
Reuters is the first media outlet to detail connections between Unitree designs and the Army program.

The episode underscores broader problems with the United States’ ability to compete with China’s state-directed manufacturing sector in high-tech strategic industries, including those critical to national security.

Backed by subsidies, clusters of component factories, and a tolerance for heavy losses, Chinese companies have seized market share across industries such as solar panels, drones, EVs and quantum communications, many of which were first developed in the U.S. with government or military backing.
Kenneally commercialized the U.S. breakthroughs through his company Ghost Robotics, which supplies U.S. special forces with advanced, ruggedized robots.
But compared to Unitree, its production is small, and costly.

stories.title: Three NATO reconnaissance planes spotted near Kaliningrad Region
stories.summary: One of them is a US Gulfstream EA-37B Compass Call II electronic warfare aircraft
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 18.

Three NATO reconnaissance aircraft have been spotted near the Kaliningrad Region from the Polish and Lithuanian sides over the past two hours, a source in European Union air traffic services told TASS.
"One of the reconnaissance aircraft, a Bombardier ARTEMIS II, arrived in the Baltic Sea area from its permanent base in Constanta, Romania.
It is currently preparing to fly in circles around the Russian region, using Polish and Lithuanian airspace as well as airspace over neutral waters in the Baltic Sea," the source said.
The aircraft was last seen in the area on August 10.
On several other occasions, the Bombardier ARTEMIS II flew over the Baltic states and along Estonia's Gulf of Finland coast without approaching the Russian or Belarusian borders.
The second aircraft was a NATO Boeing E-3A Sentry airborne early warning and control aircraft.
Registered in Luxembourg, it arrived in Poland from the Geilenkirchen military base in Germany.
"The aircraft is flying in circles at an altitude of about 9.5 kilometers in Polish airspace near Gdansk," the source said.
Two Airbus.
A330-243MRTT tanker aircraft operated by the Royal Air Force were also detected near the city.
The third aircraft was a US Gulfstream EA-37B Compass Call II electronic warfare aircraft, which reached the Baltic Sea from Powidz, Poland.

stories.title: How a year-old Hanoi crash exploded into a Gen Z campaign for justice in Vietnam
stories.summary: The fatal traffic accident took place in Hanoi more than a year ago.
article_sentences: A 2025 fatal traffic accident involving a former senior politician and an 18-year-old girl has sparked a rare public outcry in Vietnam.
Youth in Vietnam used social media campaigns and virtual memorials to demand transparency and justice, challenging official narratives and information restrictions.
The authorities responded with a state TV report explaining the outcome of investigations into the accident but warned against intentions by "hostile forces" to incite unrest and cause disorder.

In a rare move, state broadcaster Vietnam Television (VTV), in its flagship current affairs programme on Aug 17, devoted a full six-minute report to a fatal traffic accident that took place in Hanoi more than a year ago.
In a country where more than 10,000 people are killed in traffic accidents each year, such events would hardly be expected to attract much attention.

Yet this incident, involving a former senior politician, has caused a storm in the run-up to Vietnam’s National Day on Sept 2, prompting the authorities to issue an official statement on what happened.

On May 30, 2025, former Vietnamese National Assembly deputy Nguyen Sy Cuong, 64, was driving his luxury car when it suddenly veered into the opposite lane at high speed and collided head-on with an oncoming motorbike carrying a father and his 18-year-old daughter.
The collision severed the teenager’s right leg, leaving her in extreme pain and causing heavy blood loss.
The teen, Do Ngoc Phuong Thuy, was taken to hospital but died 10 days later, just days before her high school graduation examination.
The case was transferred to the Hanoi police for investigation, but no further information has been made public since then.
The last time it was mentioned in the domestic media was on May 31, one day after the accident.
After that, there was only radio silence.
